picked.title: Cracking Mobile Manipulation: From Failure Diagnosis to Agentic Robot System
picked.summary: Recent vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong performance on local robot manipulation, yet their success does not readily translate to long-horizon mobile manipulation. In our experiments, a pretrained subtask VLA achieves 80% success rate on atomic manipulation tasks but only 19% when these skills are composed into mobile manipulation. We argue that this gap stems from failures across the execution process rather than from local manipulation capability alone. To uncover these bottlenecks, we systematically diagnose failures in long-horizon mobile manipulation and identify three dominant regimes: task planning, navigation and base positioning, and local manipulation. Based on this diagnosis, we develop failure-guided agentic intervention that augments a fixed subtask VLA with demonstration-based planning guidance, adaptive visual memory, accessibility-aware base adjustment, and local end-effector adjustment. On RoboCasa365, these interventions progressively improve task success from 19% to 47%, with the finalized system reaching 49% on held-out episode seeds, compared with 18% for the baseline. The same design improves performance from 14% to 37% on BEHAVIOR-1K and from 5/20 to 13/20 on real-robot tasks. These results suggest that reliable mobile manipulation can be advanced by diagnosing and intervening on the current bottleneck, rather than uniformly scaling the underlying policy. Our code will be released at https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/Cracking-Mobile-Manipulation.git.

picked.title: DexStitch: Learning and Composing Dexterous Skills from Human Videos via Contact-Aware Robotic Inpainting
picked.summary: A long-horizon manipulation task consists of primitive skills and the transitions connecting them. Learning skills that can be executed in sequence requires supervision for both, which is costly to collect on a robot. Human videos offer a scalable source of demonstrations, but transferring them to robots requires extracting robot-compatible observations and actions together with their skill structure. We present DexStitch, a framework that cuts long-horizon human videos into skills and transitions, converts them into aligned robot observation-action-skill data, and stitches the learned skills into a requested sequence. A skill classifier first segments the videos into manipulation skills and transitions. DexStitch then converts the human demonstrations into robot observations and actions while retaining their corresponding skill labels. During conversion, per-finger human-object contacts guide dexterous hand retargeting and robotic inpainting, preserving contact geometry and finger-object occlusion ordering. To stitch the learned skills into a sequence, a shared skill-conditioned policy is pretrained on the resulting synthetic data and finetuned on a mixture of synthetic data and a small set of single-skill teleoperation episodes. Conditioning on the current and next skills guides each transition toward the following skill, while predicted skill progression enables closed-loop switching. On a held-out session, the classifier agrees with manual annotations on 92.4% of frames. Across four household skills, DexStitch achieves 80.0% single-skill success and 77.5% sequence success.

picked.title: Complementary Future Token Pruning for World Action Models
picked.summary: World action models (WAMs) jointly predict future visual states and robot actions, but processing dense future-frame tokens incurs substantial inference latency. We propose CF-Prune, a training-free framework for pruning future-frame tokens in pretrained WAMs. Our key insight is that future visual predictions support action generation and therefore need not preserve every visual detail required for high-fidelity video synthesis. CF-Prune combines instruction and action attention to identify task-relevant tokens during the initial denoising forward pass, even when future-frame and action representations remain highly noisy. An entropy-based phase identification mechanism further retains dense computation during precision phases to mitigate pruning-induced performance degradation. Experiments on RoboLab, RoboCasa, and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate consistent inference speedups. At a 35% pruning ratio, CF-Prune achieves average speedups of 1.19-1.27x while improving task success rates. At a 50% pruning ratio, it achieves 1.29-1.33x average speedups on both simulation benchmarks, with overall success rates within 1.0 percentage point of the baseline.

picked.title: Refine Actions If Needed: Adaptive Action Chunk Refinement for Robot Manipulation
picked.summary: Computationally lightweight manipulation policies predict executable actions with low inference latency, but prediction errors can limit task success. Iterative generative policies can achieve higher task success rates, but repeated network evaluations increase inference latency. Refining action proposals from computationally lightweight policies can combine these strengths, but the amount of refinement needed varies across states. We introduce RAIN (Refine Actions If Needed), a framework that predicts action errors at different refinement levels to decide whether and how much to refine each executable proposal, before performing any refinement. We train an ensemble to predict these errors by comparing action proposals and their refined versions with expert actions from offline demonstrations, without requiring explicit labels of refinement needs. Calibration balances uncertainty, computation, and temporal consistency. We evaluate RAIN on eight ManiSkill tasks and four real-robot tasks. In simulation, our policy achieves 66.6% success, approaching the best evaluated diffusion-policy success rate with 5.71 times lower policy latency. On the real robot, success increases from 55.0% with Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) to 72.5%, with comparable average successful completion time. Matched controls show that dynamic routing maintains the strongest observed fixed-refinement success level with 26.6% fewer refiner evaluations. Project page: https://rain-policy.github.io/.

picked.title: 3D Lane Detection with Odometry for High-Speed Vehicle Racing
picked.summary: Lane boundary detection is a critical component in autonomous driving systems and has been rigorously studied in regular driving scenarios. However, it is less explored in vehicle racing, where the car moves at higher speeds across more extreme road geometries. To study this problem, we introduce a new dataset for 3D lane detection in racing, featuring >250k images from multiple camera feeds and inertial measurements taken with a Lexus LC 500 driving on a closed circuit. With this dataset, we compare various approaches to 3D lane detection and propose modifications that permit frames to be processed at rates of almost 300Hz while retaining high predictive performance in the racing application. This facilitates a multi-camera ensemble approach that is validated on hardware. We show that sensing modalities such as inertial measurements can be leveraged for pre-integration to regress road geometries over both cameras and time, yielding improvements in key metrics. Compared to methods such as BevLaneDet, adding odometry and ensemble predictions improves the F1 score by 3 points and reduces near-vehicle mean absolute errors (MAEs) by >30%. We show F1 scores >0.9 and lateral MAEs of <0.18m in vehicle deployments. Image Jul 15, 2026 Human Interactive Driving Read More 1 Minute Read

picked.title: Agility chooses Nyobolt for ultra-fast charging for Digit 5 humanoid
picked.summary: Nyobolt is providing power technology for Digit 5 that enables Agility's humanoid to work up to 20 hours a day.

picked.title: 日本に本当に勝ち筋はあるのか ヒューマノイド「解剖」で見る中国の強さと課題
picked.summary: 中国では現在、ヒューマノイドロボットの開発や量産、社会実装に向けた動きが加速している。しかし、完成品の動向を追うだけでは、その競争力の源泉や本格普及に向けた課題までは見えてこない。SUGENAのセミナー「フィジカルAI解体新書」では、ヒューマノイドをAIや関節、センサー、手などに“解体”し、中国勢の強さと残された課題を解説した。本稿ではその内容を基に、日本企業が勝負できる領域を見ていく。

picked.title: 昆仑万维诞生世界上第一款消费级显卡视频大模型游戏，同步开源
picked.summary: 从"看 AI 生成视频"，到"亲手玩 AI 生成的世界"——中间隔着的，其实是一道关于"实时"的坎。 2026年10月15日，昆仑万维正式发布世界上第一款运行在单张消费级显卡上的视频大模型游戏——Matrix-Game 4.0。Matrix-Game 4.0 构建起了游戏世界模型的新范式： 由游戏引擎维护世界状态与交互规则，由视频生成模型实时呈现精细画面。 它把 480p、60 FPS 的实时游戏体验，装进了一张 NVIDIA RTX 5090；从你按下按键，到画面做出反应，延迟低于 150 毫秒。Matrix-Game 4.0 首次跑通了"代码生成游戏逻辑 → 结构画面提供结构约束 → 视频模型实时渲染"的完整闭环，让游戏原型开发、个性化定制与 UGC 从此拥有了真正可落地的技术路径。项目已同步开源。 开源地址 Huggingface：https://huggingface.co/Skywork/Matrix-Game-4.0 一、从一段代码到一个可玩的世界——Matrix-Game 4.0 的四块基石 1. 单卡实时：让"可玩的视频模型"走出实验室 在消费级显卡上实时生成游戏画面，曾是难以兼得的目标——视频生成模型对算力的胃口，长期把它锁在实验室的多卡集群里。 Matrix-Game 4.0 给出的答案是一组硬指标： 单张 NVIDIA RTX 5090，480p 分辨率下游戏以 60 FPS 运行 ；从玩家按键到首帧响应， 端到端延迟低于 150 毫秒 ；单步去噪的稳态生成速度达 83 FPS ， …
